title.zh: Anthropic私下游说美国议员推动前沿AI安全草案，设定政府干预门槛
title.en: Anthropic秘密游说国会：模型须面临超10亿美元损失或50人伤亡风险，政府才能叫停

current_state.zh: Anthropic 正在向美国议员推销一项尚未公布的草案法案，该法案将允许政府仅在某一前沿模型构成可预见的、迫在眉睫的超过 10 亿美元损失或至少 50 人死亡或重伤风险时，限制其发布或使用，同时要求定期进行独立评估，并将部分州级 AI 安全规则纳入联邦框架。
current_state.en: Anthropic is pitching U.S. lawmakers on an unpublished draft bill that would let the government restrict a frontier model's release or use only when it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of over $1 billion in damages or at least 50 deaths or serious injuries, while requiring regular independent evaluations and folding some state AI safety rules into a federal framework.

updates.what_changed_zh: Anthropic 正私下游说美国议员，推动一项前沿 AI 安全草案法案。该法案仅在模型构成超过 10 亿美元损失或 50 人以上死亡或重伤的迫在眉睫风险时才允许政府干预，且限于生物武器、失控和网络攻击场景，并要求进行独立第三方评估和获得法院批准。
updates.what_changed_en: Anthropic is privately lobbying US lawmakers on a draft frontier AI safety bill that would permit government intervention only when a model poses imminent risk of over $1 billion in damages or 50+ deaths or serious injuries, limited to bioweapon, loss-of-control, and cyberattack scenarios, with independent third-party evaluations and court approval required.

updates.background_zh: 美国目前仍没有全面的联邦 AI 法律，2025 年至 2026 年初各州出台的 AI 规则依然具有可执行性；国会已两次拒绝通过广泛的联邦优先条款。Anthropic 与 OpenAI 此前还分别推动在其实验室内部嵌入独立安全评估方，同时研究人员呼吁这类评估应保持透明与独立。
updates.background_en: The United States still has no comprehensive federal AI law, and state AI rules enacted in 2025 and early 2026 remain enforceable; Congress has twice declined to pass broad preemption language. Anthropic and OpenAI have separately pushed to embed independent safety evaluators inside their labs, amid calls from researchers for transparency and independence in such evaluations.
updates.market_impact_zh: 该草案对加密市场结构（如托管、交易所或稳定币）没有直接传导渠道；其影响主要通过 AI 概念代币的市场情绪体现，而这类代币对美国 AI 政策新闻标题的反应，通常大于对具体立法文本的反应。
updates.market_impact_en: The draft has no direct channel into crypto market structure such as custody, exchanges or stablecoins; any effect runs through sentiment toward AI-themed tokens, which tend to react to U.S. AI policy headlines rather than to specific legislative text.
